task.name: Worker shell workflow
task.objective: Execute worker workflow using direct tmux via bash: generate a prompt file, spawn a tmux session, monitor log and state files, and optionally chain to a follow-up command. When native tmux is unavailable in the current Bash tool environment, bridge into WSL with `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -- ...`. tmux-cli MCP is optional and never required.

parameters.param: Project directory passed to helper scripts. Default: current working directory.
Logical worker or slash command name. Used as prompt context and as the default worker name when no window name is provided.
Argument or task description to include in the prompt. NULL means no extra argument.
Worker and tmux session name. If not provided, derive it from COMMAND_NAME or fall back to worker.
Multi-line instructions to include in the prompt file.
Behavioral constraints prepended to the prompt.
A follow-up command to execute after successful completion.

requirements.runtime: Primary runtime: direct tmux via bash
Secondary runtime: WSL bridge via `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -- ...` plus `wslpath` path conversion
Optional transport: tmux-cli MCP only if explicitly available and proven working
requirements.note: Do not gate worker execution on `claude mcp list`, MCP health status, or "Failed to connect" false negatives.
Consumers must provide enough context to build a worker prompt.

llm.mandate: Execute steps one by one in exact order unless a failure requires fallback.
Create a TODO list for tracking all work.
Use direct shell actions and helper scripts as the primary execution path.
Fallback mode is allowed only when neither native nor WSL bridge tmux runtime is available, or tmux session creation fails.
Do not require tmux-cli MCP tools for worker execution.

step.title: Resolve runtime prerequisites
step.action: Set PROJECT_DIR to the consumer-supplied value or the current working directory.

check.condition: native tmux and native claude are available

check.action: Run `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc 'command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1'`.

check.condition: WSL tmux and WSL claude are available
check.action: Select WSL bridge tmux worker mode.
Convert Windows paths to WSL paths with `wslpath` before calling helper scripts.

check.condition: neither native nor WSL bridge tmux runtime is available
check.action: Select fallback mode and report that tmux runtime is unavailable in both environments.

step.critical: Do not run `claude mcp list` here. MCP status is not a gate.

step.title: Prepare worker identity and prompt file
step.action: Choose WORKER_NAME from WINDOW_NAME when provided. Otherwise derive it from COMMAND_NAME or use worker.
Create `.claude/tmp/` if it does not exist.
Compose the prompt from PERMISSIONS, scope guard, COMMAND_NAME, ARGUMENT, and MESSAGE.
When WSL bridge mode is selected, convert PROJECT_DIR and prompt file paths with `wslpath` before invoking runtime helpers.
step.note: If COMMAND_NAME is provided, treat it as logical task context for the worker prompt. Do not require interactive slash command loading.

check.action: Select fallback mode and report that tmux session creation failed.

step.title: Monitor progress
step.action: Use `.claude/scripts/worker-status.sh "$PROJECT_DIR" "$WORKER_NAME"` as the status source of truth.
Use `.claude/scripts/worker-tail.sh "$PROJECT_DIR" "$WORKER_NAME"` to inspect recent output when needed.
Use the worker log file, done marker, and exit code file as the completion source of truth.
step.note: Optional follow-up input may be sent with direct `tmux send-keys` to the running session if absolutely necessary.

check.condition: status is done:0 or equivalent success
check.action: Collect the final output from the log file and continue.

check.condition: status is done with a non-zero exit code
check.action: Inspect the log file, summarize the failure, and decide whether to retry, fallback, or ask the user.

check.condition: status is missing after a failed spawn or crashed session
check.action: Treat this as a tmux runtime failure and enter fallback mode.

step.title: Fallback mode
step.action: Use a non-tmux fallback only because neither native nor WSL bridge tmux runtime is available, or tmux session creation failed.
State explicitly why fallback was selected.
step.critical: Do not blame MCP health status or `claude mcp list` for entering fallback mode.

step.title: Post-completion
step.condition: POST_COMPLETION is provided and the worker completed successfully
step.note: The next worker should use the same direct tmux decision tree.

execution-rules.rule: Optional MCP integration may be used only if explicitly validated.
Worker execution must remain functional without MCP.
Prompt file generation plus `.claude/scripts/worker-spawn.sh` is the primary way to start workers.
If native tmux is unavailable in the current Bash tool environment, helper scripts must bridge through `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -- ...` and convert Windows paths with `wslpath`.
Source of truth: `.claude/logs/*.log`, `.claude/worker-state/*.done`, `.claude/worker-state/*.exit`, and optional `tmux capture-pane`.

llm.critical-rules: - This is a worker task that coordinates with real tmux sessions, not MCP-only tooling. - If native tmux and claude exist, use native tmux worker mode. - Otherwise prefer WSL bridge tmux worker mode before any fallback. - Do not inspect `claude mcp list` as a gating condition. - Do not require tmux-cli MCP tools for worker execution. - Convert Windows paths to WSL paths with `wslpath` when bridge mode is selected. - Fallback only when neither native nor WSL bridge tmux runtime is available, or tmux session creation fails. - Create a TODO list at the start and track the run to completion.
